vignette:
Carlos is a 75-year-old retired quality assurance engineer who has spent the last few decades living a quiet life in a small coastal town in Latin America with his wife, Maria. Their home, once filled with laughter and the scent of freshly cooked meals, now carries an air of tension. The walls are adorned with family photographs, capturing moments of joy that feel distant to Carlos. Though he was always the pragmatic type, approaching problems with the precision of a QA engineer, the aftermath of a devastating hurricane has left him grappling with a reality that feels increasingly unmanageable.

The storm hit on a fateful night, a night that Carlos can recall in vivid detail. He remembers the wind howling like a wild beast, shaking the very foundation of their home. As the power flickered, he sat with Maria in the living room, their hands clasped tightly together, a silent vow to endure whatever was coming. The roof eventually gave way, raining debris upon them. In that moment, fear gripped him, a primordial instinct rising to the surface as he shielded Maria with his body, praying for the storm to pass. When the winds finally calmed and dawn broke, the landscape was unrecognizable—trees uprooted, homes submerged, and their own house left in shambles.

In the months that followed, Carlos struggles to find a new normal. The physical damage to their home has been repaired, but the emotional scars run deeper. He feels as though he is constantly walking through fog, his thoughts muddled with images of the storm. Whenever the wind picks up, a familiar dread washes over him. He often finds himself staring out of the window, watching the trees sway, his heart racing as if he is back in that harrowing moment. He has started avoiding conversations about the hurricane, and when friends invite him to gatherings, he declines, preferring the safety of solitude. The once vibrant man who shared stories and laughter now sits in silence, a mere shadow of his former self.

Carlos’ sleep is fragmented, punctuated by nightmares that replay the chaos of that night. He wakes drenched in sweat, his heart pounding, grasping for the reassuring presence of Maria beside him. She often comforts him, but he feels like a burden. He does not want her to see the fear that has taken root in his heart, nor does he want to admit that he no longer feels safe in his own home. During the day, he distracts himself with mundane tasks, but his mind drifts back to the storm, the sound of the wind, the feeling of helplessness, and the guilt that washes over him for not being able to protect Maria more effectively.

At work, Carlos tries to maintain his routine. Though he retired last year, he has been helping out a local tech start-up, offering insights based on his decades of experience. However, he finds it increasingly difficult to concentrate. The technical reports he once breezed through now feel insurmountable. His colleagues, eager to engage, notice his distraction, but he deflects their concerns, laughing off his lapses as mere old age. Inside, he feels like a failure, unable to meet the standards he had set for himself.

As days turn into weeks, Carlos feels the weight of the storm’s aftermath pressing down on him. He carries a constant sense of anxiety, a nagging worry that another disaster could strike without warning. This fear seeps into his everyday life, affecting his relationship with Maria. On the rare occasions they go out, he becomes hyper-vigilant, scanning the sky for signs of impending storms. He can see the concern in Maria’s eyes as she tries to coax him back into the world, but the memories are suffocating.

Carlos longs for the days when he could enjoy the simple pleasure of a sunny afternoon without the specter of the hurricane looming over him. He yearns to feel the warmth of the sun on his skin without the cold grip of fear constricting his chest. As he sits at his kitchen table, staring at the remnants of breakfast, he realizes that he is trapped in a cycle of unrelenting memories, a prisoner of the past. Yet, there's a flicker of hope buried deep within—a desire to reclaim his life and to find a way back to the man he used to be.
